final_prompt:
We're choosing a vector database and need a recommendation we can act on, not a survey of every product. "Us" isn't defined yet, so start by using the AskUserQuestion tool to ask me, in one round of at most five questions, about the things that decide the answer: what the workload is (RAG, semantic search, recommendations), the expected vector count and dimensionality, query latency and QPS targets, whether we already run Postgres or another datastore, whether we self-host or want managed, and budget. If I answer "don't know" to any, pick a sensible default, state it, and carry on.

Then research current options using web search and each vendor's own docs and pricing pages, since this space changes quickly and your memory of it may be out of date. Cover pgvector, Qdrant, Weaviate, Milvus, Pinecone, and Chroma. Add one more only if you find strong evidence it belongs. For each candidate, establish from a source you actually read: the index types and scale limits, filtering and hybrid (keyword plus vector) search support, the managed and self-hosted options, the licence, and the pricing model. Don't state a benchmark number unless you can cite where it came from, and say when a figure is vendor-published. If you can't confirm a claim, mark it unverified rather than filling the gap.

This is research only. Don't create files, install anything, or change anything in this directory. Work directly rather than spawning subagents unless the sources prove too large to read in one context.

Reply with: a comparison table of the candidates, a recommendation of one primary choice and one runner-up with the reasons tied to my answers, the main risks of the primary choice, and a source link for each factual claim. Open with a one-line progress note before you start researching. Finish with a short recap, and write nothing after it.

You're done when the reply contains the table, the recommendation with risks, and the sources, and every figure in it is either cited or marked unverified.
